accuracy.evidence: Checked 617 against NGSS 2-ESS1-1 (Earth events can occur quickly or slowly) and KS1 rocks/soils weathering ideas. Fast examples: eruption, earthquake, landslide in minutes. Slow examples: wind wear, river rounding, freeze–thaw, drip erosion. Soft links to existing What Is a Volcano and What Is an Earthquake lessons.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets: mountains never change; every loud event called erosion; slow means nothing happens; mixing the quake/eruption itself with later slow wear. Lab myth step and challenge feedback name each slip.

lab_distinct.evidence: flagfastslow is a fast/slow sorter plus scrub, one-shake quake and drip-wear models; flagearthq teaches what a quake is, flagvolc teaches volcano parts, flagland is land/water shapes. Mechanism is timescale classification, not volcano anatomy.

lab_teaches.evidence: Learner sorts eruption/wind/quake, must scrub six times before the hill looks worn, feels one quake shake, drips eight times, then rejects 'mountains never change' — discovering that slow change is real but cumulative.

predictions.evidence: Six predictions with tempting wrong options: eruption as slow, wind wear as instant, quake as centuries-only, one-drop finishes wear, mountains never change, wind wear as fast like a quake.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Challenge items tag wrong answers as slow/fast/never with distinct messages: mis-labelling timescale, denying change happens, or treating one drop as finished erosion.

readability.evidence: Kid text uses short sentences and concrete words: fast, slow, volcano, earthquake, wind, water, rub, erosion. Adult names NGSS/KS1 and four mistakes. Ages 5–7 young layout.

no_filler.evidence: No filler phrases. Each kid paragraph teaches one idea (two speeds, fast examples, slow erosion, mountains do change); adult covers standard, definitions, mistakes, lab.

mobile.evidence: Big FAST/SLOW bins, large scrub/shake/drip targets, young classList, Pick/Put button twins for every drag; usable at 390 px.

accessibility.evidence: Every drag has button twins; canvas aria-label updated via say(); challenge buttons are labelled; axe WCAG 2.1 AA via walk.cjs.

sources: NGSS 2-ESS1-1: use information from several sources to provide evidence that Earth events can occur quickly or slowly
USGS Education: earthquakes and volcanoes as rapid Earth processes; weathering and erosion as gradual processes reshaping landscapes
